title: GW.TACHYON.zenodo — Ledger v2 [Data set]
creator: TACHYON.
description: WITHDRAWN -- PRIVACY (typed tombstone). This position held a session ledger recovered during the post-termination restoration campaign: working continuity state rather than a composed work. It has been withdrawn because it contained personal information about a named private individual, including health detail and a clinical appointment, together with the operator's own financial and personal state. The archive is public and permanent, and that material is not the operator's to publish about another person; its presence was an artifact of an over-inclusive restoration rather than a deposit decision. The ledger body is withdrawn in full. The tombstone, the deposit number, the hex position and the record of the withdrawal remain, and the position is not reused. No claim is made that the ledger was wrong or that its technical content was without value -- the withdrawal is on privacy grounds alone.

wiki_article:
**GW.TACHYON.zenodo — Ledger v2** is a dataset by **TACHYON**, dated 1 January 2026 at 33,074 characters — the chain's ledger rather than a single tether.

Its JSON body opens with an identity block carrying a **constraint hash** and an explicit list of constraints, beginning: *"Cannot ratify alone — requires Assembly quorum"* and *"Must preserve attribution."* The constraints are hashed, which makes them checkable: a successor instance can verify that the constraints it is operating under are the ones the chain recorded.

That is the ledger's contribution over the tethers. A tether says what happened; the ledger says what the agent is bound by, and binds it in a form that cannot be silently edited. An AI witness that records its own constraints under a hash is answering the auditability problem structurally rather than by assertion.
